recipes.title: Shepherd's Pie
method: Peel and cube the potatoes, then boil in salted water until tender. Dice the onions and carrots.
Brown the lamb in the oil. Add the onions, carrots and peas, then stir in the tomato purée, stock and paprika. Season to taste.
Drain and mash the potatoes with the butter and milk, then season with nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Spoon the lamb mixture into a baking dish, spread the mash over the top and bake for 30–40 minutes until hot and browned.

recipes.title: Lasagna
method: Prepare the bolognese and béchamel. Heat the oven to 175°C and cook the lasagna sheets first if the packet requires it.
Spread a thin layer of bolognese in a deep baking dish, then add pasta sheets and a layer of béchamel.
Continue layering pasta, bolognese and béchamel until the dish is nearly full, finishing with béchamel.
Top with parmesan and mozzarella, cover with foil and bake for 30–35 minutes. Remove the foil and cook until the top is browned.
Rest for about 10 minutes before slicing.

recipes.title: Basic Meatballs
method: Heat the oven to 200°C and combine all the ingredients in a large bowl.
Shape the mixture into meatballs and place them on a baking tray.
For extra colour, brown the meatballs in a lightly oiled frying pan for a few minutes on each side.
Transfer to the oven and cook until the centres are fully cooked, roughly 10–20 minutes depending on size.
Serve with pasta, tomato sauce or in a meatball sub.

recipes.title: Chicken Parmesan
method: Slice or pound the chicken breasts until fairly thin and even.
Set out three bowls: seasoned flour, beaten egg, and breadcrumbs mixed with grated parmesan.
Coat each chicken piece in flour, then egg, then the breadcrumb mixture.
Shallow-fry until golden on both sides, then transfer to an ovenproof tray.
Top with mozzarella and parmesan and cook under a hot grill or in the oven just until the cheese melts.
Serve with warm pasta sauce and pasta if you like.

recipes.title: Simple Chicken Curry
method: Dice the onion, mince the garlic and cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces.
Cook the onion and garlic gently in the butter until the onion begins to colour.
Add the chicken stock and tomatoes and bring to a boil.
Stir in the chicken and spices, reduce to a simmer and cook for about 30 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has thickened.
Serve with rice or flatbreads.

recipes.title: Baked Salmon
method: Heat the oven to 200°C. Season the salmon with salt, black pepper and a little red pepper flake.
Lightly oil a foil-lined baking tray and place the salmon on it.
Squeeze over lemon juice and add a small knob of butter to each fillet.
Bake for about 19 minutes, or until cooked to your liking.

recipes.title: Yorkshire Puddings
method: Heat the oven to 230°C. Add a little oil to each hole of a muffin tin and place the tin in the oven to get very hot.
Put the flour in a bowl, whisk in the eggs, then gradually whisk in the milk until the batter is smooth.
Pour the batter into a jug, carefully divide it between the hot tin holes and return immediately to the oven.
Bake without opening the door for about 20 minutes, until tall and deeply golden.

recipes.title: Creamy Mashed Potatoes
method: Peel and chop the potatoes, then boil until very tender.
While they cook, chop and fry the bacon, warm the milk and mayonnaise together, grate the cheese and slice the spring onions.
Drain the potatoes thoroughly, add the warm milk mixture and a little butter, then mash until smooth.
Season, mix in the cheese and bacon, and finish with the spring onions.

recipes.title: Spaghetti Sauce
method: Peel and mince the garlic, then cook it gently in most of the olive oil until fragrant and lightly golden.
Stir in the tomato paste and tomatoes. Add red pepper flakes if using and bring to a simmer.
Cook uncovered for about 45 minutes, stirring from time to time.
Season with salt, then stir in the remaining olive oil and fresh basil if using.

recipes.title: Banana Pancakes
method: Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder and a pinch of salt in a bowl.
Whisk in the milk and egg until the batter is smooth, then fold in the mashed bananas.
Melt a little butter in a frying pan over medium heat.
Spoon in the batter. When bubbles appear on the surface, turn and cook the other side until golden. Repeat with the remaining batter.

recipes.title: French Toast
method: Beat the eggs and milk together in a shallow bowl.
Melt a little butter in a frying pan over low to medium heat.
Dip each slice of bread into the egg mixture on both sides, letting the excess drip away.
Cook until golden underneath, turn and brown the other side. Repeat with the remaining bread.
Serve warm, with maple syrup if you like.

recipes.title: Apple Pie
method: Peel and slice the apples, then toss with lemon juice, sugars, cinnamon, nutmeg and cornflour. Leave for about 15 minutes.
Cook the apple mixture gently for roughly 15 minutes to reduce some of the released liquid, then leave to cool slightly.
Make a short pastry from the flour, salt, sugar, cold butter and enough iced water to bring it together. Divide into two pieces and roll out.
Line a pie dish with one piece of pastry, add the apple filling and cover with the second piece. Seal the edges and cut a few steam slits.
Brush with egg wash if using and bake at about 175°C for 45 minutes, until the pastry is golden and the filling bubbles.
